name: St Francis Xavier Cathedral
reason: Rule 2 church test met: Wikivoyage Geraldton names the Romanesque interior by Monsignor Hawes, open weekdays and free, with an adjacent Hawes museum; the Coral Coast board page calls it one of Hawes' masterpieces with paid guided tours.
objection: A working cathedral; the visit is architecture-only and the tours run on set days, so a half-hour visit relies on the interior being open.

name: HMAS Sydney Memorial
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Geraldton and the Coral Coast board both name the HMAS Sydney II Memorial on Mount Scott; a major national memorial with a hilltop view over the city, not a plaque.
objection: It is a war memorial (rule 3 excludes minor memorials) and the stop is often under half an hour; the shown name should be 'HMAS Sydney II Memorial'.

name: Museum of Geraldton
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage and the Coral Coast board name it (WA Museum branch, Shipwrecks Gallery with Batavia and Zuytdorp relics, daily highlights tour); open daily.
objection: Small regional museum; the Wikipedia title redirects, so views understate nothing either way.

name: Geraldton Esplanade
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage (breakwater stroll with sea lions) and the Coral Coast board (landscaped walkways and viewing platforms over the city) both name it; a waterfront walk, second tier.
objection: Essentially a town foreshore promenade; a visitor in a hurry would not detour for it, and it overlaps the foreshore playground area.

name: Old Geraldton Gaol
reason: Rule 1 one source only: Wikivoyage says the cells are preserved inside what is now a craft centre (weekdays and Saturday morning).
objection: For: preserved 19th-century cells open to look around. Against: one counted source, a craft shop in the building, short visit, limited hours; the board page does not mention it.

name: Geraldton Regional Art Gallery
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage lists hours and rotating contemporary exhibitions in the former town hall; the Coral Coast board tells visitors not to miss it. A public gallery visitors go into.
objection: No permanent collection, so the draw depends on what is showing; a city gallery of regional standing.

name: Point Moore Lighthouse
reason: Rules 1 and 2 split: Wikivoyage and the Coral Coast board both name the 1877 candy-striped tower (Australia's tallest metal lighthouse), but there is no public access to the tower except occasional open days.
objection: For: an iconic photographed landmark two sources name, with windsurfing at Point Moore beside it. Against: exterior-only most of the year (rule 2), a short look.

name: Back Beach
reason: Rule 1 two sources but only as a surf break: Wikivoyage calls it Geraldton's most popular surf spot, the board a good break for beginners.
objection: For: a beach named by two visitor sources. Against: a suburban surf beach no source recommends as a stop beyond surfing; friend test 'only if nearby'.

name: St Georges Beach
reason: Rule 1 two sources but only as a windsurfing spot (Wikivoyage Do, Coral Coast board's windsurf list).
objection: For: named twice. Against: a suburban beach 4 km north of town listed only in activity lists; not a place visitors are sent to see.

name: Utakarra Racecourse
reason: Rule 4: a race-meeting venue, only of interest on race days (Oct-April meetings); otherwise nothing to see.
objection: Attendance is free and it is a permanent venue, but the draw is the event, not the place.

name: Port Denison
reason: Town rule: the Coral Coast board gives 'Dongara - Port Denison' its own destination page (marina, Harbour Beach, South Beach, Thungara Trails, drive-in); Wikivoyage Dongara describes its beaches.
objection: Twin town with Dongara: keep as one place with Dongara (the board treats them together), not two spots; duplicate risk with a Dongara candidate.

name: Big Lobster
reason: Quirky roadside icon rule: Wikivoyage Dongara lists the giant fibreglass rock lobster at the highway turn-off as a sight.
objection: A 10-minute photo stop with one source; its 8621 page views are almost certainly the South Australian Big Lobster (Kingston SE) and must not be read as this one's score.

name: Irwin District Museum
reason: Rule 1 one source: Wikivoyage Dongara lists the small museum in the 1870s courthouse, police station and jail.
objection: For: heritage buildings with a museum inside, on the Dongara Heritage Walk. Against: open only Mon-Sat 10-noon, small, one source; a local-history stop.

name: Russ Cottage
reason: Rule 3: a single 19th-century cottage maintained by the Irwin District Museum and one of 28 stops on the Dongara Heritage Walk; part of a larger place, no opening details.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it separately and the board names it on the heritage walk.

name: Irwin River Trail
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage describes the 4.6 km boardwalk loop along both banks of the Irwin; the Coral Coast board describes the Thungara Trails along the Irwin River banks. A walk two sources name.
objection: A town-edge riverside walk; the board names it as part of the Thungara trail set rather than by this name, and the estuary crossing is tide-dependent.

name: Dongara Nature Reserve
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage only notes it is a duneland area at the edge of town; no source names anything to do there; a local reserve.
objection: It is listed under See on Wikivoyage.

name: Greenough Leaning Tree
reason: Quirky roadside icon rule: the Coral Coast board's Greenough page calls the Leaning Trees of Greenough a popular icon with a purpose-built photo parking area; Wikivoyage Mid West pictures it.
objection: A short photo stop; the name should be the plural 'Leaning Trees of Greenough' (several trees on the Greenough Flats, one signed pull-out).

name: Kalbarri Skywalk
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA's Kalbarri page leads with it and Wikivoyage and the board name it; the park's best-known view.
objection: Shares the West Loop car park with Nature's Window: keep both distinct (platforms vs arch).

name: Z-Bend
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage, DBCA (Z Bend Lookout and river trail) and the board name it; lookout walk plus a hike into the gorge.
objection: None strong; one of several Murchison Gorge lookouts.

name: Ross Graham Lookout
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage (350 m trail to the river), DBCA (Ross Graham River Walk, own entry station) and the board name it; the only easy access to the river in the gorge.
objection: Second-tier compared with the Skywalk and Z-Bend; a short stop.

name: Hawk's Head Lookout
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage, DBCA (Hawks Head, own entry station) and the board name it; a gorge lookout with picnic area.
objection: 2 km from Ross Graham and sharing its entry road; could be argued as one stop with it.

name: Nature's Window
reason: Rules 1-3: the board says the park is best known for Nature's Window and the Skywalk; DBCA and Wikivoyage name it. The iconic rock arch over the gorge, a distinct feature reached on foot.
objection: Same car park as the Skywalk and on The Loop trail; the script suspected it is part of the Skywalk spot. It is a different feature (an arch, not the platforms).

name: The Loop, Kalbarri
reason: Rules 1-3 arguable: DBCA promotes the 9 km Loop trail past Nature's Window and Wikivoyage names the Loop; but as described (the loop drive and car park) it overlaps Nature's Window and the Skywalk.
objection: For: a named DBCA day hike. Against: near-duplicate of Nature's Window (rule 3) and closed after 7am Nov-Mar; if kept, keep it as 'The Loop Trail' (the hike), not the car park.

name: Natural Bridge (Kalbarri)
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage calls it the highlight of the coast; DBCA lists Natural Bridge - Castle Cove and the boardwalk to Island Rock.
objection: None strong.

name: Red Bluff, Kalbarri
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage (beach, Wittecarra Creek landing site) and DBCA (Red Bluff, Red Bluff Beach) name it; beach, cliffs and lookout.
objection: Possible overlap with a Jakes Point candidate (the board's own page) at the same beach's north end.

name: Mushroom Rock
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage and DBCA name it, with a 1.5 km loop trail along the coast.
objection: Its loop runs through Rainbow Valley, so the two are one walk.

name: Rainbow Valley
reason: Rule 3: duplicate of Mushroom Rock; the Mushroom Rock loop passes through Rainbow Valley's striated rocks (Wikivoyage lists them in one sentence).
objection: DBCA lists Rainbow Valley as its own site; if Mushroom Rock is dropped, Rainbow Valley would be the one to keep. Note the name collides with the NT Rainbow Valley.

name: Eagle Gorge
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage and DBCA name the lookout and beach trail, start of the Bigurda Trail.
objection: A coastal lookout among several on the same road.

name: Port Gregory
reason: Town wrapper rule: the board's page is about the Pink Lake (Hutt Lagoon) at Port Gregory; the village itself is a small fishing village whose draws are the lagoon and the Lynton convict station beside it.
objection: For: the board calls it a popular fishing and diving holiday village with a reef. Against: town listed beside its own attraction (Hutt Lagoon); keep the lagoon, mention the village.

name: Zuytdorp Cliffs
reason: Rule 1-2 arguable: Wikivoyage names the 150 km cliff line north of Kalbarri, but access is a long 4WD track and the wreck site is off-limits.
objection: For: a dramatic named coast with a famous wreck story. Against: one source, no named access point or thing to do, long linear feature; most visitors see it only at Steep Point or from the air.

name: Kalbarri Pelican Feeding
reason: Rule 4 arguable: Wikivoyage and the board describe the daily 8:45 am pelican feeding at the Grey Street foreshore; a daily custom at a permanent place, not an event, but timed.
objection: For: two sources, a daily ritual like the Monkey Mia feeding. Against: it is an activity, not a place (the place is a grassy foreshore), and there is nothing to see outside that half hour.

name: Chinaman's Beach
reason: Second-tier beach rule: Wikivoyage and the board name it as Kalbarri's safe family swimming beach on the river mouth.
objection: Small in-town patch of sand; friend test weak.

name: Blue Holes, Kalbarri
reason: Rules 1-2: the board calls Blue Holes renowned for snorkelling (protected fish habitat) and Wikivoyage lists the stone basins; a beach with something to do.
objection: An in-town beach; second-tier.

name: Rainbow Jungle
reason: Rule 2 closed: Wikivoyage says it was not open in 2022, and listings since mark the birdpark closed (destroyed by Cyclone Seroja in 2021); nothing confirms it reopened.
objection: Lonely Planet still lists it, but that listing predates the cyclone.

name: Northampton
reason: Town rule: the Coral Coast board gives it its own page with the Hampton Road Heritage Walk (37 buildings), Chiverton House Museum and Hawes churches; a National Trust historic town.
objection: Mainly a gateway passed through to Kalbarri and Horrocks; its draws are modest.

name: Horrocks Beach
reason: Second-tier beach rule: the board gives Horrocks its own page (Tourism Australia's #1 mainland beach 2018, reef, Willigully Caves rock art, Little Bay).
objection: One counted source; the Wikipedia title is the settlement, so name and photo must be the beach/settlement consistently.

name: Chapman Valley
reason: Rule 3/feature-or-area: a farming shire, not a single place; the board page lists scattered features (Mills Lookout, Chapman River Nature Trail, a fishing park) rather than a place to go.
objection: The board treats it as a destination and it is a wildflower drive in season; named features inside it could be candidates on their own.

name: Shark Bay World Heritage Discovery Centre
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage (Denham and Shark Bay) sends visitors here first for the World Heritage interpretive exhibits; a museum-style centre with a half-hour-plus visit.
objection: It is a visitor centre; both Wikivoyage pages carry identical text, so they are one source in practice.

name: Blue Lagoon Pearl Farm
reason: Operator/shop rule: Wikivoyage calls it primarily a sales pitch; a pearl business visited by boat tour, not a place.
objection: It does give an insight into pearling.

name: Little Lagoon, Denham
reason: Second-tier beach rule: Wikivoyage names it and the board's Denham page notes it was #5 in Tourism Australia's Top 10 beaches 2025, reached by the Nicholson Point trail.
objection: Mostly a paddling pool for families.

name: Ocean Park Aquarium
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage and the Coral Coast board name it (rescued turtles and sharks, continuous guided tours); daily, paid.
objection: The two 'counted' Wikivoyage pages are identical text, but the board is an independent second source.

name: Hamelin Pool Marine Nature Reserve
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage and the board name the living stromatolites, an obvious draw.
objection: The board says the stromatolite boardwalk is currently closed; they can still be seen from the Hamelin Pool quarry. Name the spot 'Hamelin Pool' (the place visitors name) and check for a duplicate Hamelin Pool candidate.

name: Faure Island
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage says boat trips pass it but do not land; a conservation reserve with no public access.
objection: Notable conservation island; dugong trips go near it.

name: Wooramel Seagrass Bank
reason: Rule 2: an underwater prairie in open water, seen only incidentally from boat trips; no place to stand or go.
objection: World Heritage feature named by Wikivoyage.

name: Eagle Bluff
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage and the board (100 m clifftop boardwalk with turtles and rays below) name it.
objection: A roadside lookout; shorter than half an hour for many.

name: Useless Loop
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage says the company salt town is off-limits to casual visitors.
objection: Its high page views reflect the name's curiosity.

name: Steep Point
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage and the board's Denham page name the westernmost point of the mainland; a destination in itself for 4WD travellers.
objection: 4WD only and remote; one formal counted source (board mentions it in passing).

name: Dirk Hartog Island
reason: Rules 1-2: the board gives it its own page (national park, Cape Inscription, campsites, eco lodge) and Wikivoyage lists it.
objection: Reached only by booked barge, ferry or flight.

name: Bernier and Dorre Islands
reason: Rule 2 unclear: Wikivoyage mentions them only for their history (the 1908-09 lock hospitals) and access via Carnarvon; no source names anything a visitor does there.
objection: For: two Wikivoyage mentions, a national park, historic significance. Against: no visitor activity or landing arrangement described; likely a reject unless a DBCA page shows public access.

name: Shark Bay Marine Park
reason: Rule 3: an umbrella marine reserve whose draws (Monkey Mia dolphins, Hamelin Pool, dugongs) are their own places; not a place to go in itself.
objection: The board has a page for it.

name: Cape Range National Park
reason: Rules 1-2: its own Wikivoyage page and DBCA page; a flagship park of the Ningaloo Coast World Heritage Area.
objection: None; the script's part-of signal is about its features, which are separate candidates. DBCA currently carries a Cyclone Narelle camping notice.

name: Yardie Creek
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA calls a visit 'a must' (gorge trail, boat tour), Wikivoyage names it.
objection: None strong.

name: Mandu Mandu Gorge
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage and DBCA (3 km Mandu Mandu walk) name it.
objection: None strong.

name: Turquoise Bay
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage, DBCA and the board name it as Ningaloo's best-known shore snorkel.
objection: None.

name: Oyster Stacks
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage, DBCA and the board name it as a snorkel site.
objection: High tide only.

name: Sandy Bay, Cape Range
reason: Second-tier beach rule: Wikivoyage and DBCA name it (swimming, snorkelling, kitesurfing).
objection: One of many park beaches.

name: Lakeside Beach
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage (excellent snorkelling), DBCA and the board's Ningaloo Reef page name Lakeside as a shore snorkel site.
objection: Shares an access road with Kori Bay and the Discovery Centre.

name: Kori Bay
reason: Rule 1 thin: Wikivoyage and DBCA mention it only by name and access road; nothing named to do.
objection: For: a park beach two sources name. Against: near-duplicate of Lakeside on the same access road, no stated activity.

name: Mangrove Bay
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage and DBCA name the Mangrove Bay bird hide.
objection: A bird hide is a short stop for most.

name: Milyering Discovery Centre
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage and DBCA name the park visitor centre with displays and audiovisuals on the park and reef, daily, free.
objection: A visitor centre; arguably part of Cape Range National Park rather than a separate draw.

name: Osprey Bay
reason: Rule 3 arguable: Wikivoyage calls it Sandy Bay's continuation with a campground; DBCA lists its campground and kayak trail.
objection: For: a DBCA kayak snorkel trail. Against: near-duplicate of Sandy Bay and mostly a campground.

name: Bloodwood Creek Lookout
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA (snorkelling, swimming, whale watching, lookout platform over the creek system) and Wikivoyage name it.
objection: A lookout-plus-beach among many in the park; second tier.

name: Ningaloo Reef
reason: Rules 1-2: the board's Ningaloo Reef page and Wikivoyage Exmouth name it; a World Heritage reef reached straight off the beach.
objection: Long linear feature: pin at its main access, and its snorkel spots are separate candidates.

name: Vlamingh Head Lighthouse
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage Exmouth names it as a popular sunset and sunrise lookout on the North West Cape, with WWII radar remains on the hill.
objection: One counted source; the tower itself is not open.

name: Jurabi Turtle Centre
reason: Rule 1 one source: Wikivoyage says it facilitates seasonal viewing of nesting turtles beside the lighthouse.
objection: For: a permanent interpretive centre for the Ningaloo turtle season the board promotes. Against: one counted source, the draw is seasonal (Nov-Mar) and at night.

name: Point Murat
reason: Rule 2, no public access: Wikivoyage Exmouth says Murat Road past the Bundegi turn-off is closed to all but authorised vehicles and the point is beside the naval station; the only public draws there are Bundegi Beach and the Navy Pier dive, judged as their own entries.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it first under See (the cape tip), but what it describes visitors doing is the pier dive and the beach, not the headland.

name: Navy Pier, Exmouth
reason: Rule 2 arguable: Wikivoyage Exmouth and Gascoyne both name the Navy Pier dive, a renowned shore dive, but the pier is a working navy pier with access only on regulated dive trips with one operator (Dive Ningaloo). Case for: the place itself (the pier and its reef life) is the draw, as Kapiti Island is reached only by permit boat. Case against: certified divers only, one operator, no access otherwise, one counted source family.
objection: A place reachable only by one dive operator's trip is close to 'an operator in place of its destination'; no Tourism WA or board page was opened for it.

name: Harold E Holt Naval Communication Station
reason: Rule 2, closed: Wikivoyage Exmouth says the base is off-limits; its towers are only seen from afar.
objection: The 387 m Tower Zero is a striking landmark visible from the North West Cape road, but there is nowhere public to stop for it.

name: SS Mildura Wreck
reason: One counted source (Wikivoyage Exmouth: wreck visible at low tide 80 m off the cape tip, reached by Mildura Wreck Road) and a short visit: marginal, so review. Case for: a named, signposted shore-visible wreck at the tip of the cape. Case against: a low-tide look from the shore, likely under 30 minutes, near Vlamingh Head Lighthouse.
objection: Only one counted source read; a second (DBCA or Tourism WA) would be needed for a keep.

name: South Muiron Island
reason: Rules 1-4 as the Muiron Islands: Australia's Coral Coast has a Muiron Islands page (Cod Spot on South Muiron, The Keyhole, The Gap; world-class diving and snorkelling) and Wikivoyage Exmouth names the islands as a turtle breeding ground visited by trips. Keep as one spot named 'Muiron Islands' (the place the dive boats go), not South Muiron alone.
objection: Reached only by dive and snorkel boats from Exmouth, and the draw is underwater; uninhabited reserve islands you do not tour on land.

name: Krait Memorial
reason: Rule 3, minor memorial: Wikivoyage Exmouth tells the Operation Jaywick story at length, but the site is a memorial near Learmonth jetty with nothing else to do.
objection: The history is genuinely interesting and the guide spends a paragraph on it; a WWII-interest visitor might stop.

name: Potshot Memorial
reason: Rule 3, minor roadside memorial: Wikivoyage Exmouth gives it one line ('on the main highway approaching Learmonth Airport').
objection: A guide does name it, which is the roadside exception, but with no detail of anything to see.

name: Learmonth Solar Observatory
reason: Rule 2: a working scientific facility; Wikivoyage Exmouth says 'No tours'.
objection: None worth stating: exterior only.

name: Shothole Canyon
reason: Rules 1-4: DBCA Explore Parks has a current Shothole Canyon page (12 km 4WD scenic drive along the canyon floor, 'one of the most rugged areas of Cape Range') and Wikivoyage Exmouth and Cape Range NP list it. The 2022 post-fire closure that Wikivoyage reports is not on DBCA's current page, so it is open.
objection: 4WD only, and Wikivoyage's closure note (Feb 2022) is older than DBCA's page; confirm on DBCA park alerts at research time.

name: Charles Knife Canyon
reason: Rules 1-4: DBCA Explore Parks has a current Charles Knife Canyon page (winding drive to the top of the range, Charles Knife and Thomas Carter lookouts over Exmouth Gulf, the 6 km Badjirrajirra walk) and Wikivoyage Exmouth lists it. Two counted sources, real things to do.
objection: Wikivoyage still says the area was closed after the 2022 wildfire; DBCA's page no longer says so, but check alerts. Overlaps Shothole Canyon (the two meet at their heads), though they are separate drives with separate entrances.

name: Fig Tree Cave
reason: Rule 2, closed: Wikivoyage Exmouth says the access road crosses private farmland and since 2020 the landowners have closed public access.
objection: A decorated cave a guide names, with a rope-ladder descent, would be a strong draw if access reopened.

name: Ningaloo Aquarium
reason: Rules 1-4: Wikivoyage Exmouth lists it with prices and daily hours, and Australia's Coral Coast has a product page for the Ningaloo Aquarium and Discovery Centre in the Ningaloo Centre (live marine and land animals, regional history). A daily-open paid attraction.
objection: Likely the same place as a 'Ningaloo Centre' candidate if the run has one: keep one spot, not two. Wikivoyage's hours ('9AM-4:30AM') are garbled; research hours afresh.

name: Exmouth Town Beach
reason: One counted source with one line ('the long sandy strip by Mantarays'), so marginal: review. Case for: the town's beach, a second-tier beach stop. Case against: Wikivoyage says nothing to do there and points snorkellers to Cape Range beaches; the town's own beach adds little beside Bundegi and the Cape Range beaches.
objection: A one-line mention is the weakest kind of counted source.

name: Coral Bay Beach
reason: Rules 1-4: Wikivoyage Coral Bay calls the main beach 'very beautiful, maybe the most beautiful around' with shore snorkelling on Ningaloo Reef, and Australia's Coral Coast's Coral Bay page names the coral gardens 'mere metres from the white sandy beach'. The beach on Bill's Bay is the headline thing to do in Coral Bay.
objection: Possibly a near-duplicate of Coral Bay itself (the town is the beach); if Coral Bay is a spot or destination, this may be its headline spot or folded into it. The near-shore coral died in 2022 per Wikivoyage.

name: Paradise Beach, Coral Bay
reason: One counted source (Wikivoyage Coral Bay: quieter rugged beach around the headland, start of the drift-snorkel back to the bay), arguable as distinct: review. Case for: a named second-tier beach with its own snorkel route. Case against: 200-500 m from the main beach, effectively part of the Coral Bay Beach visit, and Wikivoyage says its coral is dead since 2022.
objection: Near-duplicate of Coral Bay Beach.

name: Lookout Point, Coral Bay
reason: Rule 3, part of a larger spot: a dune at the end of the town's car park overlooking the main beach and Paradise Beach; Wikivoyage Coral Bay itself says Coral Bay has few views and this gives 'a decent overview'. A ten-minute look belonging to the Coral Bay Beach visit.
objection: The guide does name it, which is the named-pull-out exception.

name: Five Fingers Reef
reason: Rules 1-4: Wikivoyage Coral Bay recommends it as the best shore snorkelling near Coral Bay (live coral, reef sharks, turtles, stingrays within 100 m of shore), and Australia's Coral Coast's Coral Bay page names Five Fingers Reef among its 4WD snorkelling spots. Two counted sources.
objection: 4WD only (deep soft sand), or a 1-2 hour walk from town.

name: Shark Sanctuary, Bill's Bay
reason: Seasonal natural phenomenon at a place (brief: may be kept, season noted), one counted source (Wikivoyage Coral Bay: young tiger sharks in the shallows Nov-Jan, viewed from shore on a 1-2 km walk). Case for: a distinctive wildlife sight at a named place. Case against: only one source, seasonal and condition-dependent (high tide, calm day), and the place is the north end of Bill's Bay, part of the Coral Bay shore.
objection: Outside Nov-Jan there is nothing specific to see beyond the beach walk.

name: Maud's Landing
reason: One counted source and a short visit: Wikivoyage Coral Bay names it as the original landing, 'nice beach but breezy and no coral'. Case for: a named beach with history 3 km north of town. Case against: the guide's own description is lukewarm; locals' dog beach.
objection: Faint praise from the only source; leans reject.

name: Pinnacles Desert Discovery Centre
reason: Rule 3, part of a larger spot: the discovery centre is the visitor centre at the start of the Pinnacles Desert drive and walk (DBCA: 'Just behind the visitor centre is the Pinnacles View Lookout'); the Pinnacles Desert spot covers it.
objection: DBCA and Wikivoyage both describe exhibits worth time (displays, soundscapes, videos), and it has fixed hours, so it could be a museum-type stop; mention it in the Pinnacles bio.

name: Hangover Bay
reason: Rules 1-4: Wikivoyage Nambung NP lists it (white sand, snorkelling, swimming, dolphins and sea lions) and Australia's Coral Coast's Cervantes page names it for snorkelling, surfing and windsurfing. A second-tier beach with two counted sources.
objection: One of many beaches on this coast; mostly a local picnic spot.

name: Kangaroo Point, Cervantes
reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Nambung NP; Australia's Coral Coast Cervantes page) but both describe a boat-launch and shore-fishing beach with picnic shelters, 'usually strewn with seaweed' (Wikivoyage). Case for: named by both, with kangaroos and emus. Case against: a boat launch and picnic area more than a beach visitors travel to.
objection: Hangover Bay is the better beach in the same park.

name: Cervantes Islands
reason: Rule 3, part of a larger spot: the sea-lion haul-out islets off Cervantes lie inside Jurien Bay Marine Park (Wikivoyage Nambung: the marine park runs from Green Head to Nambung's boundary) and boat trips do not land. The place visitors go is the marine park (kept separately).
objection: Wikivoyage names the islands specifically as what the Cervantes sea-lion trips visit.

name: Buller, Whittell and Green Islands
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage Nambung says landing is not allowed on Buller or Whittell and the Green Islands are off-limits in the seabird season; low scrubby islets with nothing to do, inside the marine park.
objection: None worth stating.

name: Grey (Cervantes)
reason: Rule 2/3: an off-grid squatter shack community (Wikivoyage Nambung); the source names it for its history, not as somewhere to visit, and it has no public attraction.
objection: A curiosity some 4WD visitors pass through on the way down the coast.

name: Lobster Shack, Cervantes
reason: Brief: a business is a place only when a visitor source singles it out. Australia's Coral Coast's Cervantes page calls a visit to Lobster Shack, the Indian Ocean Rock Lobster Factory, 'a highlight' (factory tours), and Wikivoyage names it as the base of the sea-lion trips and a lunch spot. Case for: a factory tour like a brewery tour, singled out by the board. Case against: it is a seafood restaurant and processing business and an operator base.
objection: Restaurants and operators are rejected unless singled out; the board's 'highlight' is the only thing lifting it.

name: Lancelin
reason: Brief, towns: Tourism WA has a Lancelin place page and Australia's Coral Coast lists it; visitors base themselves there for kitesurfing, windsurfing and the sandboarding dunes. A beach town with its own draws.
objection: Its main draw (the dunes) is a separate candidate; the town must not be a wrapper for it (COVERAGE: a town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw). Its beaches and windsurfing are the town's own.

name: Lancelin Sand Dunes
reason: Re-looked for a counted source: Tourism WA has an attraction page for the Lancelin Sand Dunes (sandboarding on 45-degree dunes, the biggest in WA, panoramic outlook over town and coast, 2 km system). An obvious draw with a counted source; activity well over half an hour.
objection: Business News reports the dunes shrinking with sand mining; parts are used by 4WD and buggy operators. Not near-duplicate of Lancelin if the town keeps its beaches.

name: Jurien Bay Jetty
reason: One counted source (Wikivoyage Jurien Bay: 162 m fishing and strolling jetty, built 2011) and a short visit. Case for: the town's named sight, a jetty walk. Case against: a 20-minute stroll, and the board's Jurien Bay page does not name it.
objection: Leans toward folding into Jurien Bay's bio.

name: North Head, Jurien Bay
reason: Rules 1-4: Wikivoyage Jurien Bay lists it (scenic peninsula, wartime radar station remains), and Australia's Coral Coast's Jurien Bay and Sandy Cape pages describe the well-preserved WWII radar installation (two intact igloo shelters, foundations, underground tank) with walk trails. Two counted sources, a headland with heritage to walk around.
objection: 4WD only, and the board treats it as an add-on to Sandy Cape.

name: Drover's Cave National Park
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage Jurien Bay says many caves are screened off, and its 'must-see', Stockyard Gully, is a separate park (Australia's Coral Coast lists Stockyard Gully National Park near Leeman). Nothing a visitor can do in Drovers Cave NP itself is named; the second listed source is only the board's home page.
objection: Two sources name it as a park; if a DBCA page shows open caves or walks, it would need another look.

name: Stockyard Gully
reason: Rules 1-4: named by Wikivoyage Jurien Bay, Australia's Coral Coast (Stockyard Gully National Park page and Leeman, Eneabba pages), Tourism WA (Stockyard Gully Caves) and Lonely Planet: a 300 m walk-in limestone cave on an old stock route. Name it 'Stockyard Gully Caves' or the national park.
objection: 4WD only, the cave floods in wet periods, and a torch is needed.

name: Boullanger Island
reason: Rule 2/3: Wikivoyage Jurien Bay names it for the dibbler but says there is little reason to land on the marine park's islands; it is part of Jurien Bay Marine Park, which is kept.
objection: The largest and closest island, seen from town.

name: Sandy Cape, Jurien Bay
reason: Rules 1-4: Australia's Coral Coast has its own Sandy Cape page (sheltered white beach, swimming, snorkelling, sandboarding, Grigson's Lookout nearby) and Wikivoyage Jurien Bay lists it. A second-tier beach with two counted sources.
objection: A campground beach 13 km north of Jurien Bay; the board says it has become popular on social media.

name: Jurien Bay Marine Park
reason: Rules 1-4: Australia's Coral Coast has a Jurien Bay Marine Park page (sea lions, 21% of WA's population breed here) and a sea-lion page, and Wikivoyage Jurien Bay and Nambung describe the limestone ridge reached by boat for snorkelling and diving. The place the sea-lion swims go, as a spot.
objection: A large marine area experienced through boat operators; pin and bio must be the marine park, not a tour, and it absorbs the Cervantes Islands and Boullanger Island.

name: Leeman
reason: Brief, towns: Australia's Coral Coast gives Leeman its own page with its draws (Point Louise surf break and snorkelling reef, windsurfing, kayaking bays, base for Stockyard Gully and Lake Indoon).
objection: A small cray-fishing town; most visitors pass through on Indian Ocean Drive.

name: Badgingarra
reason: Australia's Coral Coast gives it a page, but its draws are mostly outside the town (Badgingarra National Park trail, Watheroo NP's Jingemia Cave); in town, the 4.2 km art trail and the Vern Westbrook heritage walk. Case for: own board section, wildflower base. Case against: a roadhouse farming town, mostly a spring wildflower stop.
objection: Brief keeps towns given their own section; the in-town draws are thin.

name: Dandaragan
reason: Australia's Coral Coast page names only a church seen for its soapstone and arch, Aggie's Cottage (used by craft groups) and a scenic drive; the wildflowers are in Lesueur NP. Case for: own board section. Case against: nothing named to do for half an hour in the town itself.
objection: Leans reject.

name: Eneabba
reason: Australia's Coral Coast's Eneabba page points to a caravan park's wildflower walks, nearby lakes (Indoon, Logue) and Tathra and Stockyard Gully national parks; nothing in the town itself. Case for: own board section and Carnamah-Eneabba wildflower drive. Case against: its draws are separate places.
objection: Lake Indoon has its own board page and may be the better spot.

name: Coorow
reason: Australia's Coral Coast page names Coorow Farm's 1.2 km wildflower walk and drive (a board product page too) and stargazing lakes; seasonal wildflowers are the draw. Case for: own section, a named walk at the farm. Case against: a small farming town, a spring-only stop; the farm walk, not the town, is the draw.
objection: If kept, the spot may be the Coorow Farm wildflower trail rather than the town.

name: Carnamah
reason: Brief, towns: Australia's Coral Coast gives it a page with draws in town: the giant Chamberlain tractor sculpture (a 'Big Thing' quirky roadside icon), the 700 m art and heritage trail, MacPherson Homestead and Yarra Yarra Lakes stargazing.
objection: A small wheatbelt town, mostly a wildflower-season stop; its museum opens only on Friday afternoons.

name: Carnamah Museum
reason: Rule 2/3: re-looked for a counted source; Australia's Coral Coast's Carnamah page names it but says it opens only on Fridays 1:30-5 pm, so it is not there for most visitors, and it is a local-history collection that belongs in the Carnamah town spot.
objection: The board does name it (a counted source now exists); a heritage-stone building with farm machinery on display.

name: Three Springs
reason: Brief, towns: Australia's Coral Coast gives it a page with named draws: the heritage walk and Duffy's Store, the Talc Mine Lookout over the largest talc mine in the southern hemisphere, nearby pink lakes and Yarra Yarra Lakes.
objection: A small town, best in the wildflower season; the pink lakes are seasonal.

name: Mingenew
reason: Brief, towns: Australia's Coral Coast calls it 'the true heart and soul of Wildflower Country' with Mingenew Hill lookout, Depot Hill Reserve, the historical walk, a museum (board product page) and stargazing; base for Coalseam Conservation Park.
objection: Mostly a spring wildflower stop.

name: Urawa Nature Reserve
reason: Rule 1 too thin: Wikivoyage Mid West only lists the name in a sentence about Mullewa, with nothing to see or do; Australia's Coral Coast's Mullewa page does not name it. A local wildflower reserve.
objection: It is a counted source naming it; in spring it may have good wildflowers.

name: Coalseam Conservation Park
reason: Rules 1-4: DBCA Explore Parks page (wildflowers, Irwin Lookout, Plateau Loop Trail, exposed coal seams and fossils, campgrounds) and Australia's Coral Coast (Mingenew and Mullewa pages call it a wildflower highlight). Two counted sources, walks and lookouts.
objection: Mainly a spring destination; outside wildflower season the views and geology remain.

name: Coral Coast Highway
reason: A spot is a place: a highway route (Geraldton to Exmouth) that links the region's places, each judged on its own.
objection: The board brands it as a touring route with its own page.

name: Indian Ocean Drive
reason: A spot is a place: a coastal touring road; the board's Indian Ocean Drive pages are a heading for its towns and beaches (Cervantes, Jurien Bay, Sandy Cape, Leeman), which are judged separately.
objection: A named scenic drive with its own Wikipedia article and board section, comparable to a coastal road some apps list.

name: Wildflower Country
reason: Region brand, not a place: the board's heading for the inland wildflower towns, each judged on its own.
objection: Could be a destination name for the proposer (a tourism brand travellers use), but not a spot.

name: Gascoyne Junction
reason: Gateway village whose draw is the journey beyond it (Pipiriki benchmark): Australia's Coral Coast's page is mostly about Mount Augustus and the Kennedy Range; in town only a museum collection and a picnic pergola. Case for: own board page, the base for Kennedy Range NP. Case against: its draws are the parks.
objection: Also hosts the Gassy Dash (an event, not a reason).

name: OTC Dish, Carnarvon
reason: Rules 1-4 as the Carnarvon Space and Technology Museum: Wikivoyage Gascoyne lists the OTC Dish (tracked Gemini and Apollo), and Australia's Coral Coast's Carnarvon page and its OTC Dish and museum product pages describe interactive displays, an Apollo capsule simulation and planetarium, open daily.
objection: Probably the same place as a 'Carnarvon Space and Technology Museum' candidate: keep one spot under the museum's name.

name: Gassy Dash
reason: Rule 4: an annual off-road rally (March/April) on the Gascoyne riverbed, an event.
objection: None.

name: Quobba
reason: Australia's Coral Coast's 'Quobba and Red Bluff' page and Wikivoyage Gascoyne name the Quobba coast (fishing, surfing, snorkelling, Quobba Station stays). Case for: a named remote coast. Case against: it is an area and a station (accommodation), and its specific places, the Quobba Blowholes and Point Quobba lagoon, and Red Bluff, are separate candidates kept here.
objection: Risk of a wrapper: keep the blowholes and Red Bluff rather than the area.

name: Red Bluff, Gascoyne
reason: Rules 1-4: Australia's Coral Coast calls The Bluff a 'world-renowned' surfing spot with a big left-hand reef break and has a Red Bluff page; Wikivoyage Gascoyne names it for surfing. A distinct place on the coast.
objection: Run as part of Quobba Station (camping and shacks), remote, and mostly a surfers' and anglers' stop.

name: Gnaraloo
reason: Rules 1-4: Australia's Coral Coast has a Gnaraloo Coast page (Tombstones surf breaks, Gnaraloo Bay and 3 Mile Lagoon coral snorkelling, turtles), and Wikivoyage Gascoyne names it for surfing. A remote coast with things to do.
objection: Station-run and remote (self-sufficiency needed); camping only at set camps.

name: Westernmost Point of Oceania
reason: Rule 1: re-looked; no counted source names it. The OpenStreetMap node sits on the west coast of Dirk Hartog Island (-25.589, 112.921), a marker point, not a visitor site; the place visitors go is Dirk Hartog Island or Steep Point (the mainland's westernmost point, with its own board page).
objection: A superlative point some 4WD visitors seek out.

name: Seaview Cottage, Drummond Cove
reason: Rule 1/2: re-looked; no counted source, only an OpenStreetMap heritage building (alt name Mary Drummond's Cottage) with no sign it is open to visitors.
objection: A heritage-listed early cottage near Geraldton.

name: Island Rock
reason: Duplicate of Natural Bridge: Australia's Coral Coast covers 'Natural Bridge and Island Rock' as one stop with shared lookouts at Castle Cove, and Wikivoyage Kalbarri lists them in one listing. Keep as one spot (Natural Bridge, with Island Rock in its bio or name).
objection: Island Rock is the sea stack in many Kalbarri photos and is named separately by both sources.

name: Pot Alley
reason: Rules 1-4: Australia's Coral Coast has its own Pot Alley page (an ocean gorge on Kalbarri's coastal cliffs with a 400 m rocky trail down to a secluded beach), and Wikivoyage Kalbarri lists it. A named second-tier coastal stop with a walk.
objection: One of a string of Kalbarri coastal-cliff stops; swimming not recommended.

name: Skipjack Point
reason: Rules 1-4: Australia's Coral Coast has its own Skipjack Point page (two viewing platforms over sharks, rays, dugong and dolphins; the 1.5 km Wanamalu Trail to Cape Peron), and Wikivoyage Denham names it. A distinct lookout and walk in Francois Peron NP.
objection: 4WD only; check it is not the same spot as a Cape Peron candidate (the trail joins them).

name: Quobba Blowholes
reason: Rules 1-4: Australia's Coral Coast (Quobba and Red Bluff page: water up to 20 m, on sealed road 75 km north of Carnarvon) and the Carnarvon Visitor Centre (Shire day pass for the Point Quobba Blowholes Eco Reserve, with the Aquarium lagoon 1 km south). Two counted sources; blowholes plus a snorkelling lagoon.
objection: A shire day pass is needed; best on a rising low-to-medium tide.

name: Bundegi Beach
reason: Rules 1-4: DBCA's Cape Range NP page lists Bundegi ('a popular beach for swimming, snorkelling, kayaking and fishing'), Tourism WA has an attraction page, and Wikivoyage Exmouth names it. A second-tier beach with three sources.
objection: Also a boat ramp; a short drive from Exmouth.

name: Dalgaranga Meteorite Crater
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-golden-outback. It lies 75 km west of Mount Magnet in the Murchison inland, which the regions brief assigns to the Golden Outback.
objection: On its merits it would be a review (a small signposted crater on a station, one shire source).

name: Yalgoo
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-golden-outback. Australia's Golden Outback lists Yalgoo and Paynes Find as its destination, and the town is in the Murchison inland the regions brief assigns there.
objection: On its merits it would be a review or keep (a gold-rush town with a courthouse museum and the Hawes chapel).

name: Sunset Beach, Western Australia
reason: Rule 1: the state tourism board Australia's Coral Coast has a See & Do page for it (australiascoralcoast.com/products/sunset-beach, opened): 'one of the most popular Geraldton beaches for windsurfing and kite surfing', with toilets and car park. Rule 2: windsurf/kitesurf (hire and lessons in town), surfing, watching the sails, a 30-minute beach walk back to the town centre; open access. Rule 3: distinct beach in Geraldton's northern suburbs. Rule 4: permanent. Second-tier beach a real source names: keep. Show it as 'Sunset Beach' with wiki 'Sunset Beach, Western Australia'.
objection: One counted source; Wikivoyage Geraldton only mentions it as a bus destination, not in See/Do; the waves suit experienced riders, so for a typical visitor it is a suburban beach among several Geraldton beaches (Back Beach, Town Beach, Tarcoola) that may be near-duplicates in function.
